issues.description: SealSaloon.totalOrders type differs between specification and reference implementation: the UML in problem_statement.md specifies the field as "totalOrders: int", but the solution declares it as "private long totalOrders" and provides "public long getTotalOrders()". This creates an API/type expectation mismatch that can break tests or confuse students about the required counter type and getter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align spec and code: either change the solution to use int (field and getter) or update the UML/specification to declare totalOrders as long (and note the corresponding getter type).

issues.description: Contradiction in the problem statement about whether SealSaloon.stock is static: the task text explicitly says the "stock" attribute must be static (shared across instances), but the UML diagram shows "stock" as a normal association/attribute without any static marker. This ambiguity can lead students to implement an instance field while tests (and the reference solution) expect a static shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Make UML and text consistent by marking stock as static in the UML (e.g., {static} / underlined) and explicitly stating it is static final (or remove the static requirement from the text if instance stock is intended).

issues.description: Contradiction in the problem statement about whether SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery and SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice are static: the UML lists them as instance methods, while the task text explicitly requires both methods to be static. The reference solution implements both as static, so students following only the UML may implement the wrong API and fail tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML to mark acceptSupplyDelivery and calculateTotalPrice as static (or remove the static requirement from the text) so all artifacts and tests agree on the method type.
